newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel welcomes Yeltsin wish for closer EU ties.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel welcomes Yeltsin wish for closer EU ties.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Sunday welcomed President Boris Yeltsin's desire to strengthen ties with Europe, after the Russian leader said on Saturday he wanted his country to join the European Union.

Yeltsin said in a surprise announcement after a two-day summit in Helsinki with U.S. President Bill Clinton that he wanted Russia to be finally recognised as a full European state and that the country was prepared to join the EU.

"Firstly, a partnership agreement Russia has with the European Union, which I did a great deal to get off the ground in 1994, must be implemented now without delay," Kinkel said in a statement issued by his ministry.
Germany is Russia's closest ally in the West and has worked hard for closer cooperation with its former Cold War foes.

Kinkel said that on the basis of the agreement "the many opportunities for political and economic cooperation" should be exploited to the full before embarking on the next stage -- the creation of a free-trade zone with Russia.
Less effusive about Yeltsin's new stated aims, the European Commission, the EU's executive body, said on Saturday it had taken note of Yeltsin's remarks.

A Commission spokesman said Yeltsin's statement may be discussed at an EU foreign ministers' meeting on Monday and he pointed out that relations were currently based on a co-operation agreement which had not been ratified yet.
